projects.title: Assessing the fragility of Global Supply Chains for 3 everyday consumer products
projects.desc: Supply chain fragility, spatial concentration, labor inequality, environmental externalization. Three products compared using a composite Fragility Index. ArcGIS Pro + SAS Viya methods. Key findings: iPhone highest fragility (HHI driven), T-Shirt highest wage ratio, avocado highest water stress. Spatial diagnostic framework as contribution.

projects.title: Where Medicare is working and where it isn't
projects.desc: How do the structural incentives of the American healthcare system produce geographic concentrations of fraud, poor outcomes, and coverage gaps — and what can spatial analysis reveal about where alternative models would have the most impact?

projects.title: Mapping out the biggest war on the planet: between ants
Turning the tide for North Carolina's costal communities
projects.desc: Examines how rising sea levels are reshaping life, livelihoods, and landscapes across eastern North Carolina's coastal communities. It documents the environmental and socioeconomic challenges these areas face as they adapt to encroaching water and a changing climate.

projects.title: WCPSS Students Using GIS Collection
projects.desc: A collection showcasing how Wake County Public School System students are applying GIS in their classrooms and communities. It gathers student-created stories that demonstrate practical, real-world geospatial learning both in school and out.

projects.title: Seven Wonders of the World
projects.desc: An interactive tour of the Seven Wonders of the World, blending mapping and narrative storytelling. Fittingly, it was inspired by a Fleetwood Mac song, giving the geography lesson a musical framing device.

projects.title: Tracking grocery stores prices across the Triangle area in North Carolina
projects.desc: What started as a personal budgeting exercise became a data-driven look at how grocery prices vary by store and neighborhood in the Raleigh–RTP area. It moves past the usual anecdotal "this store is cheap/expensive" talk by tracking real staple-item prices across retailers.

projects.title: Behind CAPS MUN 2025: Building Model UN with GIS + AI
projects.desc: Showcases how 29 student organizers built CAPS MUN 2025, the first GIS integrated Model UN Conference in the United States. It highlights how the team wove GIS and AI tools into event planning and logistics, making it as much a tech story as an event recap.

projects.title: How GPS revolutionized marine science
projects.desc: Explores how GPS technology transformed the way scientists navigate and study the ocean. Co-authored with Maddie Townsend, it traces this shift through the ArcGIS storytelling format of maps, text, and imagery.

projects.title: Rediscovering Raleigh's Lost Freedmen Villages.
projects.desc: Uncovers the largely forgotten African American freedmen villages of Raleigh, communities founded by formerly enslaved people after emancipation. It works to preserve their places, people, and stories before they fade further from public memory.

projects.title: Geography At Work collection
projects.desc: A collection built around the idea that "geography connects and powers the world around us," showing spatial thinking applied to real jobs and everyday life. Rather than treating geography as an abstract subject, it curates stories on how it shows up across industries and professions.

projects.title: Growers across North Carolina collection
projects.desc: A collection highlighting agricultural producers across North Carolina through map-based storytelling. It uses location data to turn individual grower profiles into a broader narrative about the state's farming community.

projects.title: Learning by Mapping: A New Kind of Curriculum How youth used GIS to learn in a different way and map America's food supply chains.
projects.desc: Documents how youth used GIS as an alternative learning tool to map and understand America's food supply chains. It shows how GIS can be used as an interdisciplinary tool to learn about the world and how it can connect back to students' passions and their interests or fields of study that they plan on pursuing.

projects.title: Researching Raleigh's Neighborhoods and Communities
projects.desc: Brandon's first StoryMap project, and the winner of GIS Day 2024, it focuses on "measuring Raleigh's policies, places, and paths" to build more vibrant communities.It functions as a research tool examining neighborhood characteristics and municipal policy to spot opportunities for improving quality of life citywide.

learning.title: Google Photorealistic 3D Basemap Now Available in ArcGIS Online
learning.take: Photorealistic 3D scenes in StoryMaps will change how community presentations feel — policy problems become tangible when you can walk through a neighborhood in 3D.

learning.title: The 15-Minute City: Network Analysis vs. Euclidean Distance in Walkability Scoring
learning.take: Using road network distance instead of straight-line radius makes walkability scores far more accurate — I need to update the scoring in my neighborhood analysis.

learning.title: Place-Based GIS Education Increases Spatial Retention by 38% in Middle School Students
learning.take: Connecting GIS to students' own neighborhoods — not abstract datasets — is the core finding, validating everything we've been doing with 4-H curriculum in Wake County.

learning.title: Food Desert Identification and Grocery Access Gaps in North Carolina's Rural Counties
learning.take: 11 Wake County census tracts meet the USDA food desert definition — the methodology maps directly onto NOURISH and gives us a defensible framework for advocacy.

learning.title: AI-Assisted Crop Disease Classification from Drone Imagery at 94% Accuracy
learning.take: The training pipeline they used for strawberry leaf disease detection is essentially what we explored in the supply chain project — worth cross-referencing.
